Updated assessment incorporating the Beige Book:

- FOMC stance: Labor market strengthening, moderate growth, inflation below 2%, policy still accommodative with gradual hikes expected; balance-sheet normalization “relatively soon.”
- Beige Book cross-check (June 2017): Economic activity expanded across Federal Reserve Districts, with consumer spending rising. Labor markets tightened for both low- and high-skilled positions, with reports of qualified worker shortages and upward wage trends. Hiring increased in several districts, and energy activity improved alongside oil and natural gas gains. These observations broadly reinforce the FOMC’s description of solid job gains and moderate growth.
- Offsets: The latest SLOOS points to softer demand in CRE and consumer credit (autos, credit cards) and some tightening in consumer lending standards; foreign banks report tighter C&I and CRE standards. Financial stability commentary notes elevated valuations and higher nonfinancial business leverage, arguing for vigilance.
- Net: Beige Book evidence of broad-based expansion, rising consumer spending, and tighter labor markets nudges the outlook modestly more positive than a read based on SLOOS alone, though mixed credit conditions temper the upgrade. Policy remains supportive, but below-target inflation and soft loan demand cap near-term momentum.
